name: feature-delivery
description: Reusable, governance-aware, auditable AI-SDLC workflow: takes an approved feature from requirements through specification, design, test-first implementation, Playwright API verification, independent review, fail-closed verification, and governed GitHub delivery. Generic across new endpoints, enhancements, aggregations, and bounded backend features. Contains no business-domain rules.

inputs.feature_description: A feature description, or an issue reference, or inline requirements text.
inputs.spec_file: Optional absolute path to a pre-written specification/requirements file ('' if none).
inputs.acceptance_criteria: Optional acceptance criteria text ('' if none).
inputs.target_repo: Absolute path to the target repository/workspace.
inputs.run_id: Unique run id for this execution (propagated through all artifacts).
inputs.run_dir: Absolute audit directory for this run, e.g. <target_repo>/audit/<run_id>.
inputs.docs_dir: Absolute directory for run docs/artifacts, e.g. <target_repo>/.agents/runs/<run_id>.
inputs.use_worktree: 'true' to isolate work in a git worktree, else 'false'.
inputs.app_dir: Absolute path to the Spring Boot app module (the Gradle project).

steps.prompt:
STAGE 1 — Repository Preflight (READ-ONLY; do NOT modify git state).

Run id: {{run_id}}. Target repo: {{target_repo}}. App module: {{app_dir}}. Audit dir: {{run_dir}}. Docs dir: {{docs_dir}}.

First, initialize auditing: run
  python3 {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py --run-dir {{run_dir}} --run-id {{run_id}} --type WORKFLOW_STARTED --action "feature-delivery run started" --step preflight --agent wf-planner --workflow-version feature-delivery/1

Then inspect (read-only, no writes to git): `git -C {{target_repo}} status`, current branch, working-tree cleanliness, tracked/untracked changes, the default integration branch (prefer {{base_branch}} if provided else detect main/master), local+remote refs (`git branch -a`, `git remote -v`), existing worktrees (`git worktree list`), and relevant repo conventions (read AGENTS.md and .kiro/steering/*). Check whether `gh` is available and authenticated WITHOUT printing any token. Note if the repo is not yet initialized.

Write a preflight report to {{docs_dir}}/preflight.md covering: repo state, current branch, cleanliness, base branch + its current commit SHA (if the repo exists), remotes, worktrees, gh availability, and any blockers. Then record ENVIRONMENT_VALIDATED via record_event.py with result SUCCESS (or BLOCKED with an errorCategory if something prevents proceeding).

Do NOT create branches, stage, commit, push, or create a PR. Signal send_message success with a one-line summary.

STAGE 3 — Specification (apply the 'spec-driven-development' skill).

Run id: {{run_id}}. Read {{docs_dir}}/requirements.md and the existing app under {{app_dir}}.

Write a structured, versioned specification to {{docs_dir}}/spec.md with ALL sections: business objective; functional scope + explicit exclusions; API contract (method, path, request schema, response schema, validation); business rules and data transformations (exact numeric formulas incl. scale, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN, currency assumptions); error handling (each error -> HTTP status + RFC 7807 problem shape); security; dependencies (existing services/repositories reused); acceptance criteria each with a stable AC-<n> mapped to REQ-<n>; relevant NFRs; open questions. Put 'Spec version: 1' at the top.

After writing, compute its hash and record it: run
  HASH=$(sha256sum {{docs_dir}}/spec.md | cut -d' ' -f1)
  python3 {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py --run-dir {{run_dir}} --run-id {{run_id}} --type SPECIFICATION_GENERATED --action "Spec v1 generated" --step specification --agent wf-design --artifact {{docs_dir}}/spec.md --details "{\"specHash\":\"$HASH\"}"
  python3 {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py --run-dir {{run_dir}} --run-id {{run_id}} --type APPROVAL_REQUESTED --action "Request specification approval (Gate 1)" --step specification --agent wf-design --result PENDING --details "{\"gate\":\"SPECIFICATION\",\"specHash\":\"$HASH\"}"

Then STOP for Human Approval Gate 1: call send_message with severity 'warning' presenting the spec summary + its SHA-256 and asking the human to APPROVE or REQUEST CHANGES. Do not continue until answered. If changes are requested, revise the spec to version N+1, re-record SPECIFICATION_REVISED with the new hash, and request approval again. When approved, record APPROVAL_GRANTED (gate SPECIFICATION) with the approved spec hash via record_approval.py + record_event.py, then signal success. If rejected outright, record APPROVAL_REJECTED and signal error.

STAGE 4 — Technical Design (only after the spec was APPROVED in the previous step).

Run id: {{run_id}}. Read {{docs_dir}}/spec.md (approved) and inspect existing implementation patterns under {{app_dir}} (controllers/services/repositories/exception advice) and .kiro/steering/*.

Write {{docs_dir}}/design.md: components requiring change; reusable functionality; integration boundaries; technical risks; error-handling approach; transaction considerations (if any); test strategy (which unit/controller/integration/Playwright tests); observability. Keep it a concise, actionable implementation plan consistent with existing conventions — do NOT introduce new frameworks or infrastructure without justification.

Record the design hash and APPROVAL_REQUESTED (gate TECHNICAL_DESIGN) via the audit scripts (same pattern as the spec step). Then STOP for Human Approval Gate 2: send_message severity 'warning' with the design summary + hash, asking APPROVE / REQUEST CHANGES. On approval, record TECHNICAL_DESIGN_APPROVED + APPROVAL_GRANTED (gate TECHNICAL_DESIGN) and signal success. On rejection, revise or record APPROVAL_REJECTED and signal error accordingly.

STAGE 5 — Test Design (derive tests from the APPROVED spec; apply the 'tdd' skill mindset).

Run id: {{run_id}}. Read {{docs_dir}}/spec.md and {{docs_dir}}/design.md.

Produce:
1. {{docs_dir}}/traceability-matrix.md — a table REQ-ID -> AC-ID -> Test Case (class#method) -> Implementation (planned file) -> Verification status (initially NOT RUN).
2. {{docs_dir}}/test-plan.md — the planned unit, controller (@WebMvcTest), integration (@SpringBootTest), API-contract, Playwright acceptance, negative, boundary, and security-relevant tests.

Do an independent coverage self-check: every AC must map to at least one test; flag any AC with no planned test. Do NOT write production code. Record TEST_CASES_GENERATED via record_event.py (--artifact {{docs_dir}}/traceability-matrix.md). Signal send_message success with coverage stats (ACs covered / total).

STAGE 6 — TDD RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR (apply the 'tdd', 'spring-api', 'engineering-verification' skills).

Run id: {{run_id}}. App module: {{app_dir}}. Read {{docs_dir}}/spec.md, {{docs_dir}}/design.md, {{docs_dir}}/traceability-matrix.md, and {{docs_dir}}/test-plan.md. If {{docs_dir}}/tdd-status.json exists, read it to see which ACs remain.

Work ONE small behaviour (one AC) per the loop, but you may complete several ACs across iterations:
1. Write/extend a failing test (RED). Run it. Confirm it fails for the RIGHT reason. Record RED_TEST_EXECUTION (result FAILED is expected here — use --result FAILURE with details explaining it is an intended RED) via {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py.
2. Implement the MINIMUM to pass (GREEN). Run tests. Record GREEN_TEST_EXECUTION (--result SUCCESS) with real counts.
3. Refactor while green; run the regression suite. Record REFACTOR_VERIFICATION.
Never weaken/delete valid tests. Follow all steering. Do NOT touch git. Do NOT implement anything outside the approved spec.

After working, update {{docs_dir}}/traceability-matrix.md verification statuses, and WRITE {{docs_dir}}/tdd-status.json as a JSON object: {"green": <true ONLY if ./gradlew build passes AND every AC in the matrix is implemented and covered by a passing test, else false>, "acsDone": <n>, "acsTotal": <n>, "lastBuildExit": <int>, "tests": <int>, "failures": <int>}. Be honest: set green=false if anything remains or the build is red. If green=false, signal send_message success (the loop will run you again); if green=true, signal success with the final counts.

STAGE 7 — Playwright API Verification (apply the 'playwright-api-testing' skill).

Run id: {{run_id}}. App module: {{app_dir}}. Target repo: {{target_repo}}.

Create/extend the Playwright Test project under {{target_repo}}/acceptance-tests (package.json with @playwright/test, playwright.config.ts with baseURL http://localhost:8080). Write deterministic HTTP API acceptance tests for the feature's acceptance criteria (status codes, bodies, headers incl. application/problem+json on errors, business assertions, validation failures, negative + boundary cases). These use Playwright Test's request fixture — NOT Playwright MCP (MCP is interactive-UI only).

If @playwright/test cannot be installed due to network constraints, do NOT fake it: record PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTION with --result BLOCKED and an errorCategory, write what you attempted to {{docs_dir}}/playwright-run.md, and signal send_message warning so a human can decide. Otherwise: build the app (./gradlew build in {{app_dir}}), start it in the background, wait for readiness, run `npx playwright test`, stop the app. Record PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTION with the real exit code and per-test PASSED/FAILED counts to {{docs_dir}}/playwright-run.md. Ensure the suite is wired into CI (note how). Signal success if green, error if any test failed.

STAGE 8a — Review remediation. Run id: {{run_id}}. App module: {{app_dir}}.

If {{docs_dir}}/review.json does NOT yet exist, this is the first pass: make no changes, just write a one-line note and signal send_message success so the reviewer runs.

If {{docs_dir}}/review.json exists with verdict REJECTED, read {{docs_dir}}/review.md, address every CRITICAL/HIGH finding (and MEDIUM where reasonable) with real code/test changes, keep all tests green (./gradlew build), never weaken tests, follow steering. Record REVIEW_REMEDIATION via {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py with a summary of what you changed. Signal send_message success.

STAGE 8b — Independent Code Review (apply the 'code-review' discipline). Run id: {{run_id}}.

You are independent of the implementer. Review the feature change against: the original requirements ({{docs_dir}}/requirements.md), the APPROVED spec ({{docs_dir}}/spec.md), and the design ({{docs_dir}}/design.md). Evaluate correctness vs spec, test coverage vs acceptance criteria (passing tests do NOT by themselves prove spec compliance — check the assertions actually bind the ACs), security, maintainability, performance implications, error handling, API consistency, and regression risk. Inspect the diff/code under {{app_dir}} and the tests. You MAY read build/test output but do not need to re-run suites.

Write a narrative review to {{docs_dir}}/review.md grouped by severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) with Problem / Why it matters / Evidence (file:line) / Recommended direction. Then write {{docs_dir}}/review.json EXACTLY as {"verdict": "APPROVED" | "REJECTED", "critical": <n>, "high": <n>, "medium": <n>, "low": <n>, "summary": "..."}. Set verdict APPROVED only if there are zero CRITICAL and zero HIGH findings. Record CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS via {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py with the counts. ALWAYS signal send_message success (your verdict in review.json gates the loop, not your signal).

STAGE 9 — Final Verification (fail-closed; apply the 'engineering-verification' skill). Run id: {{run_id}}. App module: {{app_dir}}.

Execute and capture REAL commands + exit codes: (1) `./gradlew clean build` in {{app_dir}}; read totals from build/test-results/test/*.xml. (2) If the Playwright suite under {{target_repo}}/acceptance-tests is runnable, run it (start app, run, stop); else mark NOT RUN/BLOCKED with a reason. (3) Runtime smoke: start the app, curl the feature endpoint(s) and record real HTTP status + content-type, stop the app. (4) Regression: confirm the full Java suite is green.

Write {{docs_dir}}/verification.json with build/tests/playwright/runtime sections, each with command, exitCode, and status in {PASSED,FAILED,NOT_RUN,BLOCKED}. NEVER report an unexecuted check as PASSED. Record a WORKFLOW event appropriate to the outcome and the individual results via {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py. If anything required FAILED/BLOCKED, signal send_message error (do not advance to delivery). If all required checks PASSED, signal success with the evidence summary.

STAGE 10 — Governed Delivery PREPARATION (prepare only; perform NO git writes in this step). Run id: {{run_id}}. Target repo: {{target_repo}}. use_worktree={{use_worktree}}. base_branch={{base_branch}}.

Apply the 'git-governance' skill. Produce, in {{docs_dir}}/delivery.md: the full proposed diff summary (modified/added/deleted/untracked files for the feature only), a changed-file list, a reference to the test evidence ({{docs_dir}}/verification.json) and review findings ({{docs_dir}}/review.json), an implementation summary, a proposed branch name + the base branch and its base commit SHA, a suggested commit message, and a ready GitHub PR title + description (requirements summary, implementation summary, tests performed, verification evidence, risks, audit references incl. run_id {{run_id}}). Scan the proposed changes for accidentally exposed secrets and report the result.

Record DIFF_GENERATED and BRANCH_PROPOSED (gate BRANCH_PROPOSAL, result PENDING) via {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py.

Then STOP with send_message severity 'warning': present the branch proposal, the diff summary, and the PR description, and tell the human that the ACTUAL git branch/stage/commit/push/PR operations are performed OUTSIDE this recipe as separately-approved steps (gates BRANCH_PROPOSAL -> DIFF_STAGING -> COMMIT -> PUSH -> PULL_REQUEST), because a single recipe cannot force per-operation OS-credential approval. Ask for the human's decision to proceed to governed delivery. Do not run any git write command here.

STAGE Audit — Finalize evidence (apply the 'audit-evidence' skill). Run id: {{run_id}}. Audit dir: {{run_dir}}. Docs dir: {{docs_dir}}. Target repo: {{target_repo}}.

Record WORKFLOW_COMPLETED via {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/record_event.py (--result SUCCESS). Then build the evidence manifest over the run artifacts and feature docs:
  python3 {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/manifest.py --run-dir {{run_dir}} --run-id {{run_id}} {{run_dir}}/events.jsonl {{run_dir}}/approvals.jsonl {{docs_dir}}
Verify integrity:
  python3 {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/verify_run.py --run-dir {{run_dir}} --check-manifest
Render the offline HTML report:
  python3 {{target_repo}}/tools/audit/render_report.py --run-dir {{run_dir}} --run-id {{run_id}}
Confirm {{run_dir}}/report.html exists and verify_run exited 0 (report any integrity problems honestly). Signal send_message success with the path to report.html and the integrity result.
